children: , the Swiss premium running and sportswear brand, rose 11.46% premarket after its 2026 Investor Day in Zurich, where it unveiled its first share buyback, an authorization to repurchase up to $1 billion of Class A shares through the end of 2029, alongside a set of multi-year financial targets. The company pointed to its balance sheet and cash generation as the basis for returning capital.

On is targeting at least CHF 5.6 billion ($7 billion) in revenue by 2029, aimed at high-teens constant-currency sales growth, a gross margin of 65% or higher, and an adjusted EBITDA margin of at least 22%. That framework implies adjusted EBITDA growth above 20% a year through 2029.

For 2026, On reiterated guidance for low-20% constant-currency growth and expects roughly 17% constant-currency sales growth in the third quarter, helped by up to $65 million in tariff refunds flowing through gross profit. Stifel and Goldman Sachs both reiterated Buy ratings, at $41 and $42 targets.

title: On Targets CHF 5.6 Billion by 2029, Buys Back Stock
